decisions.reason: The failure guard bounds the declared conservative threshold |D^{-1}|c, not |BD^{-1}|. For the proposed D, D^{-1}=[[4/3,2/3],[2/3,4/3]] and c=(1,1), so the exact threshold vector is (2,2)>theta^{-1}(1,1). Cancellation in BD^{-1} does not change that test. The adjugate and determinant bounds give V<=|D^{-1}| entrywise and c^-<=c, hence Vc^-<=|D^{-1}|c. The scalar and two-by-two guard branches, finite budget, normal-range exits and local certificate proof were checked; no edit is required.

The finite branch initialized a stored matrix from arbitrary real entries without a representation rule. It now explicitly requires stored input values and copies them under P; the separate exact branch retains arbitrary real A. No input-rounding error is silently omitted. Pivot selection, prior-L row swaps, multiplication/subtraction order and failure exits are unchanged. The direct residual theorem assumes a successful run of this procedure, so it remains valid with the same original-A identity and rho>=1.

The rejection incorrectly says no separate correctness theorem exists: thm-block-ldl-star-residual-with-actual-growth already states exact correctness and proves the block congruence in step 1.1. The confirmed nonfatal defect instead is the digest concern: a union of neighbors of a two-vertex pivot includes pivot vertices, so the literal symbolic update could reconnect deleted vertices. Restricting N(J_r) to R_r fixes it without changing any numerical step or pivot test. The exact factor identity is now cited in Remarks through justified_by, rather than asserted as an instruction.

The supplier defines fill and parents conditional on an ordering; it does not select one. The Definition now explicitly fixes pi as an input parameter before constructing its filled graphs, counts and parent paths. This is a nonfatal omitted parameter made recoverable by all existing consumers, which already fix ordered vertices. No column, ancestor or reach convention changes: reach includes its start and ancestors require at least one parent edge. Empty and singleton forests cause no selection issue.

The local F in the kernel lemma has active dimension k_r+t_r, so the previous global product W_hat_r F_r W_hat_r* omitted a required embedding. The Statement now defines F_(r,act) and its zero-padded n-by-n F_r, and identity-pads T_hat_r on eliminated coordinates. Proof step 5.1 keeps the active identity separately typed and proves padding preserves the local norm bound. Telescoping gives the same positive-sign full residual and negative-sign trailing Delta residual. Step 1.1 now also explicitly identifies the transformation product with the stored multiplier columns. This is a nonfatal missing embedding convention, not a changed estimate.

The previous induction equated the sparse column with R before establishing that structurally omitted R entries vanish. The proof now constructs the dense Schur sequence directly from B=RR*, proves all scalar pivots positive, invokes Hermitian Schur-support on that independent sequence, and obtains r_ij=0 at omitted positions. Only then does column induction prove the sparse recurrence equals R. The original Statement, complex-Hermitian scope and no-cancellation condition are unchanged; no downstream propagation is triggered. This repairs the circular proof inference without new prerequisites.

The positive-definiteness energy identity is correct, including k=1. The supplier cost theorem specifically analyzes exact scalar multifrontal Cholesky, whereas F2 and step 2.1 previously left the factorization unnamed. Both now name that procedure and preserve the supplier storage convention: allocated factor entries, including structural zeros, excluding temporary contribution arrays. Substituting n=k^2 yields the same O(k^3) work and O(k^2 log k) storage for k>=2, with the separate constant one-entry case. The Example interface is unchanged.

consumer_examinations.source_excerpt:
Assume a successful run under the real operation model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with unit roundoff $u<1$ and every exact intermediate either zero or normal. Let $M=\max_{i,j}|a_{ij}|>0$, let $S^{(k)}$ be the active matrix at stage $k$ including its current pivot row, and define the actual growth of this run by
$$
\rho=\frac{\max_{k,i,j}|S^{(k)}_{ij}|}{M}\ge1.
$$
For its computed factors and accumulated row permutation, there is a residual $\Delta A$ such that
$$\widehat QPA P^T+\Delta A=\widehat L\widehat U, \qquad \max_{i,j}|\Delta A_{ij}|\le \frac{8nu}{\theta}\rho M, \qquad \|\Delta A\|_\infty\le \frac{8n^2u}{\theta}\rho M, \qquad \|X\|_
